rules.title: California security deposit cap and return rules (AB 12)
rules.requirement: Since July 1, 2024, a landlord may charge no more than one month's rent as a security deposit; small landlords may charge two months. Deposits must be returned within 21 days with an itemized statement, and landlords must offer a move-out walk-through inspection.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent; 2 months for small landlords
rules.coverage_conditions: All California residential tenancies. Landlords who own only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total, held by a natural person, family trust, or LLC of natural persons, may charge two months' rent.
rules.exemptions: Landlords owning only two rental properties with no more than four residential units total (natural person, family trust, or LLC with all natural-person members) may charge up to two months' rent.
rules.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

sources.quoted_span: Starting July 1, 2024, many landlords may only charge one month's rent for unfurnished and furnished units

rules.title: California application screening fee cap
rules.requirement: A landlord or agent may charge an application screening fee only if a unit is available, may not exceed actual out-of-pocket costs or $30 per applicant, must give an itemized receipt, and must refund unused or unconsidered fees.
rules.key_value: $30 per applicant, CPI-adjusted annually since January 1, 1998
rules.coverage_conditions: Any landlord or agent who owns or rents out residential rental property and receives a request to rent; no building age, size or ownership limits stated.
rules.quoted_span: In no case shall the amount of the application screening fee charged by the landlord or their agent be greater than thirty dollars ($30) per applicant. The thirty dollar ($30) application screening fee may be adjusted annually by the landlord or their agent commensurate with an increase in the Consumer Price Index, beginning on January 1, 1998.

rules.title: Ronald V. Dellums Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance
rules.requirement: Rental housing providers may not inquire about, require disclosure of, or use criminal history in advertising, applications, tenant selection or decisions, and may not refuse to rent, terminate a tenancy, or charge more based on criminal history.
rules.coverage_conditions: All rental housing providers in Berkeley, except lifetime sex offenders, limited public housing/Section 8 exemptions, owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units, owner move-back units, and units where existing tenants sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.exemptions: Lifetime sex offenders; public housing/Section 8 properties (limited exemptions); owner-occupied properties of 1-3 units; units under a rental agreement allowing owners to move back under BMC 13.76.130 A.9; units where existing tenants sublet or add/replace roommates.
rules.penalty: Administrative fines of at least $1,000 and up to $10,000 per violation; civil damages including actual damages or three times one month's rent, punitive damages, attorneys' fees and costs, and injunctive relief.
rules.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

sources.quoted_span: The Fair Chance Access to Housing Ordinance prohibits rental housing providers in Berkeley from asking about and using criminal history and/or criminal background checks in their rental housing advertising, applications, tenant selection process, or decision-making.

rules.title: Berkeley coordinated pricing algorithm ban
rules.requirement: No one may sell, license, or provide to Berkeley landlords, and no landlord may use, a coordinated pricing algorithm that sets or recommends rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in Berkeley.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to landlords and to persons who sell, license or provide coordinated pricing algorithms, for residential dwelling units in the City of Berkeley.
rules.exemptions: Products that publish aggregated, anonymous rental data without recommending rents; products for setting rent or income limits under affordable housing guidelines; and uses for market research for project financing, appraisals, or research, testing or training for software development.
rules.penalty: Civil penalties of up to $1,000 per violation; each month and each dwelling unit is a separate violation; prevailing party recovers attorney's fees and costs.
rules.quoted_span:
It shall be unlawful for a landlord to use a coordinated pricing algorithm described 
in subsection A when setting rents or occupancy levels for residential dwelling units in 
the City of Berkeley.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act annual rent cap (Civ. Code § 1947.12)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not raise the gross rent over any 12-month period by more than 5% plus the change in the cost of living, or 10%, whichever is lower, above the lowest rent charged in the previous 12 months, and no more than twice in 12 months.
rules.key_value: 5% + CPI, or 10%, whichever is lower, per 12 months
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental property, including units in mobilehome parks, subject to the listed exemptions; caps increases over any 12-month period and allows at most two increases in 12 months.
rules.exemptions: Affordable deed-restricted housing; dormitories; housing under stricter local rent control; housing certified for occupancy within 15 years (not mobilehomes); separately alienable condos/homes owned by non-corporate owners with notice; owner-occupied two-unit properties; mobilehome owners.
rules.penalty: Owner liable for injunctive relief, damages equal to the excess rent charged, and discretionary attorney's fees, plus up to treble damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct; the Attorney General or local city attorney may enforce; three-year limitations period.
rules.quoted_span: an owner of residential real property shall not, over the course of any 12-month period, increase the gross rental rate for a dwelling or a unit more than 5 percent plus the percentage change in the cost of living, or 10 percent, whichever is lower, of the lowest gross rental rate charged for that dwelling or unit at any time during the 12 months prior to the effective date of the increase.

rules.title: Tenant Protection Act just cause eviction (Civ. Code § 1946.2)
rules.requirement: After a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied residential real property for 12 months, the owner must not terminate the tenancy without just cause stated in the written notice; for no-fault just cause the owner must give one month's rent relocation assistance or waive the final month's rent.
rules.key_value: 12 months' occupancy; 1 month's rent relocation or rent waiver
rules.coverage_conditions: Residential real property occupied 12 months or more, except housing certified for occupancy within 15 years, single-family owner-occupied homes with no more than two units or bedrooms, owner-occupied two-unit properties, separately alienable property held by non-corporate owners, and deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.exemptions: Transient and tourist hotel occupancy; nonprofit hospital, religious, extended care, licensed elderly and adult residential facilities; school dormitories; housing certified for occupancy within 15 years; single-family owner-occupied residences and mobilehomes; owner-occupied two-unit structures; separately alienable property of non-corporate owners; deed-restricted affordable housing.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply renders the termination notice void; an owner who attempts to recover possession in material violation is liable for actual damages, discretionary attorney's fees, and up to three times actual damages for willful, oppressive, fraudulent or malicious conduct.
rules.interaction: Yields to local just cause ordinances adopted on or before September 1, 2019, and to more protective local ordinances adopted or amended after that date; property is not subject to both.
rules.quoted_span: Notwithstanding any other law, after a tenant has continuously and lawfully occupied a residential real property for 12 months, the owner of the residential real property shall not terminate a tenancy without just cause, which shall be stated in the written notice to terminate tenancy.

rules.title: California security deposit limit (Civ. Code § 1950.5)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not demand or receive security exceeding one month's rent, in addition to the first month's rent paid at occupancy, and must account for and return the remainder within 21 days after the tenant vacates. Small landlords (natural persons or family LLCs owning no more than two rental properties and four units) may charge up to two months' rent, unless the tenant is a service member.
rules.key_value: 1 month's rent; 2 months' rent for small landlords
rules.coverage_conditions: Security for a rental agreement for residential property used as the tenant's dwelling.
rules.exemptions: Security collected or demanded before July 1, 2024; advance payment of six months' rent where the lease term is six months or longer; higher security for service members subject to written statement and return rules.
rules.penalty: A landlord who in bad faith fails to comply with the itemized-statement requirements is not entitled to claim any amount of the security.
rules.quoted_span: (c) (1) Except as provided in paragraph (2), (3), or (5), a landlord shall not demand or receive security, however denominated, in an amount or value in excess of an amount equal to one month’s rent, in addition to any rent for the first month paid on or before initial occupancy.

rules.title: California reusable tenant screening report requirement
rules.requirement: If a prospective tenant provides a reusable screening report, the landlord must use it.
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords screening prospective tenants in California.

rules.title: Gov. Code § 12955 income and credit screening limits for renters
rules.requirement: A landlord may not use income standards that ignore co-applicants' combined income or, with a government rent subsidy, standards not based on the tenant's rent share, and must accept verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay in place of credit history.
rules.coverage_conditions: All owners and housing providers of housing accommodations in California; applies to rental applications and tenancies, including those with government rent subsidies such as Section 8 vouchers.
rules.exemptions: Nothing limits a landlord's ability to request information to verify employment, request landlord references, or verify the identity of a person. A landlord may still make a written or oral inquiry about the level or source of income.
rules.quoted_span:
Use a person’s credit history as part of the application process for a rental accommodation without offering the applicant the option, at the applicant’s discretion, of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of the applicant’s reasonable ability to pay
the portion of the rent to be paid by the tenant, including, but not limited to, government benefit payments, pay records, and bank statements.

rules.title: AB 325 common pricing algorithm prohibition
rules.requirement: A person may not use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade, or use or distribute one to coerce another person to set or adopt a price or commercial term it recommends.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to any 'person' as defined in Section 16702, excluding the end consumer; covers those who use or distribute a common pricing algorithm that uses competitor data.
rules.exemptions: The end consumer of a product or service is not a 'person' for purposes of this section.
rules.penalty: Violation of the Cartwright Act is punishable as a crime.
rules.quoted_span: (a) It shall be unlawful for a person to use or distribute a common pricing algorithm as part of a contract, combination in the form of a trust, or conspiracy to restrain trade or commerce in violation of this chapter.

rules.title: Housing Stability Notification Act notice requirement
rules.requirement: A landlord planning to end a tenancy must give the tenant a Notice of Tenants' Rights and Resources at the same time as the Notice to quit or non-renewal, and must also submit the Notice to Quit / Non-renewal of Lease Submission Verification Form to the City.
rules.coverage_conditions: All landlords planning to end a tenancy agreement, and foreclosing owners, must provide the notice and submit the verification form to the City.
rules.exemptions: Residences in any hospital, skilled nursing facility or health facility; non-profit facilities whose primary purpose is short-term treatment, assistance or therapy for alcohol, drug or other substance abuse.
rules.penalty: Violations are enforced by Inspectional Services; 1st offense a warning, 2nd and subsequent offenses $300 per day. Failure to submit the required information may result in a fine up to $300 per day.
rules.quoted_span: The Housing Stability Notification Act requires any landlord to provide renters with a Notice of Tenant’s Rights and Resources when planning to end a tenancy agreement.

rules.title: Cambridge Fair Housing Ordinance tenant screening and source-of-income protection
rules.requirement: Landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to select applicants only if it is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants, and housing discrimination based on source of income, including Section 8 and public benefits, is prohibited.
rules.coverage_conditions: Housing and real estate transactions in Cambridge; owner-occupied two-family dwellings are exempt.
rules.exemptions: Two-family dwellings when the owner lives there.
rules.penalty: Civil fines of up to $300 for each violation; damages, expenses and other relief after a public hearing.
rules.quoted_span: Under the law, landlords, sellers and rental agents may use any reasonable standard to determine which applicants are selected, as long as that standard is applied equally and uniformly to all applicants.

rules.title: Boston Fair Chance Tenant Selection Policy
rules.requirement: Housing providers receiving DND funding or land, or with BPDA income-restricted units, may not blanket-deny applicants with arrests or convictions; they must screen case-by-case, disregard non-convictions, sealed, expunged and juvenile records and convictions over 5 years old, and not use credit scores.

rules.exemptions: Where there is a direct relationship between a conviction and the housing sought or an unreasonable risk of substantial harm to others; current criminal behavior.
rules.interaction: Yields to federal or state criminal history requirements that conflict with this policy.

rules.title: Hoboken vacancy decontrol increase cap
rules.requirement: On a tenant's voluntary vacancy of a registered apartment, the unit is decontrolled for the new tenant's initial rent, capped at a 25% increase over the last rent paid, excluding any capital improvement surcharge; decontrol is limited to once every three years.
rules.key_value: 25% over last rent; decontrol at most once per 3 years
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental apartment units registered under §155-30 that are covered by Chapter 155; decontrol requires voluntary vacancy without harassment, duress or pressure, or a legal eviction or court order.
rules.exemptions: The decontrolled apartment unit is exempt from Chapter 155 for the new tenant's initial rental only.
rules.penalty: The Board may rescind an improper decontrol, revert the rent, and prosecute the landlord under §155-21 (fine up to $2,000).

rules.title: Hoboken rent control ordinance — rent increase limits
rules.requirement: Rents are controlled at the base rent level received as of October 1, 1985; no rent increase may be charged unless allowed by this chapter, and a landlord seeking an increase must give the tenant written notice at least 30 days before it takes effect.
rules.coverage_conditions: All dwelling units, except motels/hotels, newly constructed dwellings at first rental, industrial and nonresidential/commercial property, school/college student housing, government-owned housing, buildings vacant since January 1, 1984, and multiple dwellings built after June 25, 1987 under N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1.
rules.exemptions: Motels and hotels; newly constructed dwellings at first rental; industrial property; nonresidential and commercial units; school/college student housing; government-owned housing; buildings vacant since January 1, 1984; multiple dwellings constructed after June 25, 1987 (N.J.S.A. 2A:42-84.1).
rules.penalty: Rent increases above those allowed are null and void; excess rents must be refunded or credited to the tenant.
rules.interaction: Chapter application is preempted while a governmental agency contract regulates the rents, and resumes after the contract terminates.
rules.quoted_span:
All rents for rental of housing space and services in dwellings to which this act is applicable
     are hereby controlled at the base rent level received by the landlord as of October 1, 1985, and
     no rental increases shall be hereinafter demanded, paid or accepted, except as provided in this
     chapter.

rules.title: Hoboken initial rental decontrol upon vacancy by bona fide condo/co-op owner-occupant
rules.requirement: When a bona fide condo/co-op owner-occupant vacates the unit and offers it for rental, the unit is decontrolled only to set the initial rent, which is the amount charged in the first lease after the owner vacates; the unit is otherwise fully subject to Chapter 155.
rules.key_value: initial rent = amount charged in initial lease after vacancy
rules.coverage_conditions: Condo/co-op units whose owner has continuously occupied the unit as principal residence for the previous two years and then vacates and offers it for rent.
rules.quoted_span:
In the event that an individual who qualifies as a bona fide CCOO vacates his/her condo/co-op
     unit and offers it for rental, said unit is decontrolled solely for the purpose of establishing the
     initial rent subsequent to the bona fide CCOO vacating.

rules.title: Hoboken COVID-19 temporary moratorium on rent increases
rules.requirement: From April 1, 2020 until May 7, 2022, no rent or other rental charge for property covered by Chapter 155 could be increased, including surcharges, parking, pets and deposits; deferred increases are prospective only, with no 2020 CPI increase.
rules.key_value: no rent or charge increase; 2020-04-01 to 2022-05-07
rules.coverage_conditions: All tenancies and properties covered by Chapter 155 of the Hoboken City Code.
rules.quoted_span:
A moratorium shall be in effect to prevent any increase in the amount paid in rent or any
           additional charges whatsoever by tenants covered by this chapter.

rules.requirement: A residential landlord who raises rent more than 10% on renewal of a lease with a current tenant year over year must give the tenant written disclosures — an itemized cost breakdown, whether a rent algorithm was used, notice of the right to sue, and Division of Housing contact information — before the increase takes effect.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential landlords seeking to increase rent by more than 10% upon renewal of a lease with a current tenant year over year.
rules.penalty: Fine not exceeding $1,000 per incident for failing to provide the disclosures.

rules.title: Hoboken algorithmic rent fixing prohibition
rules.requirement: A landlord renting a residential dwelling unit in Hoboken may not price fix using algorithmic pricing, meaning software, algorithms or data-sharing platforms that collect and analyze nonpublic competitor information from other lessors to coordinate, recommend or implement rental prices, lease terms or occupancy levels.
rules.coverage_conditions: Landlords renting any residential dwelling unit in Hoboken; a residential dwelling unit is any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities.
rules.exemptions: Medical/long-term care and detention facilities are excluded from the definition of residential dwelling unit.
rules.penalty: Penalties under N.J.S.A. 40:49-5, or a fine not exceeding $2,000, or community service not exceeding 90 days.
rules.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.

sources.quoted_span: Landlords who rent any residential dwelling unit (defined as any primary residence excluding medical/long-term care or detention facilities) in the City of Hoboken are prohibited from price fixing using algorithmic pricing.

rules.title: Preventing Algorithmic Rent-Fixing in the Rental Housing Market
rules.requirement: A landlord, agent or subcontractor may not subscribe to or pay a service provider that coordinates nonpublic competitor rent data, and a service provider may not facilitate agreements not to compete on rental pricing, fees or other rental terms.
rules.coverage_conditions: Applies to real estate lessors, their agents and subcontractors, and service providers, for residential dwelling units in Jersey City.
rules.exemptions: Owners of multiple properties acting exclusively on properties controlled by the same rental property owner; licensed real estate agents acting under applicable state regulations.
rules.penalty: First violation punishable under Chapter 1, Art. I, § 1-25; subsequent violations fined $100 to $2,000; each day is a separate violation; private right of action with costs and attorney fees.
rules.quoted_span:
It is unlawful for any real estate lessor, agent, or subcontractor thereof, to subscribe to, contract with, or otherwise
exchange anything of value in return for the services of a Service Provider.

rules.title: Los Angeles source-of-income discrimination prohibition
rules.requirement: A landlord may not refuse to rent, renew, or terminate a tenancy, or apply different terms, based on a person's source of income, including Section 8 vouchers and other rental assistance.
rules.coverage_conditions: All dwelling units, guest rooms, suites, duplexes, condominiums and single-family residences rented or offered for rent in the City of Los Angeles, including mobile homes.
rules.penalty: Aggrieved person may bring a civil action for injunctive relief and damages; punitive damages of at least three times actual damages or three times one month's rent, whichever is higher, plus attorney fees and costs.

rules.title: Hoboken Rent Leveling and Stabilization Ordinance — Board approval for rent increases
rules.requirement: A landlord must obtain Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board approval before imposing any rent increase, including a hardship increase. A tenant may seek a rent decrease from the Board when services, care or maintenance decline.
rules.coverage_conditions: Dwellings covered by Article II of Chapter 155, except newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, whose exemption eligibility the Regulation Officer and Rent Regulation Officer determine.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984, with eligibility determined by the Regulation Officer and the Rent Regulation Officer respectively.
rules.quoted_span:
In the event that a landlord cannot meet his operating expenses or does not make a fair return
           on his investment, he may appeal to the Rent Leveling and Stabilization Board for a hardship
           rental increase. No landlord shall impose upon any tenant an increase in rent under this
           Article without first obtaining approval with the Board.

rules.requirement: Landlords may raise rent once every 12 months by the LAHD allowable percentage. Registration, code-enforcement and smoke-detector surcharges may be passed through.

rules.title: Los Angeles Just Cause for Eviction Ordinance (JCO)
rules.requirement: A landlord may not terminate a tenancy without just cause; at-fault causes include nonpayment, lease violations and nuisance, while no-fault causes such as owner move-in or demolition require relocation assistance. Landlords may not evict where rent owed is below Fair Market Rent.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most residential properties in the City of Los Angeles not regulated by the RSO. A tenancy is covered once the tenant has lived in the unit at least six months or the original lease expired, whichever comes first.
rules.exemptions: Transient hotels, licensed care facilities, fraternity or sorority houses, owner's roommate, cooperatives under certain circumstances, some non-profit facilities for the homeless and short-term substance-abuse treatment centers, and HACLA- or government-owned properties.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (L.A.M.C. §165.00 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

sources.quoted_span: It prohibits terminations of tenancies without just cause and requires relocation assistance for no-fault evictions.

rules.title: Berkeley Ellis Act eviction relocation assistance (2026 inflationary adjustment)
rules.requirement: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires relocation assistance when a tenant is evicted so the owner can remove the property from the rental market. From January 1, 2026 the standard payment is $19,413 and the additional payment for qualifying households is $6,471.
rules.coverage_conditions: Tenants evicted under the Ellis Act so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market; payments indexed to inflation.
rules.quoted_span: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market.

sources.quoted_span: The Ellis Implementation Ordinance requires the same relocation assistance payments for tenants evicted so the owner can remove a property from the rental housing market.

rules.title: FEHA criminal history and source-of-income screening protections
rules.requirement: Landlords may not consider arrests without conviction, sealed or expunged records, or juvenile records, and may not blanket-ban applicants with criminal history. Conviction-based denial must be directly related to tenancy, and source-of-income discrimination, including refusing Section 8 vouchers, is barred.
rules.coverage_conditions: Most housing accommodations in California and most housing providers, including landlords, tenant screening companies, apartment managers, and property management companies.
rules.penalty: Remedies include out-of-pocket losses, injunctions, access to housing, emotional distress damages, civil penalties or punitive damages, and attorney’s fees.
rules.interaction: FEHA invalidates any state law to the extent it purports to require or permit unlawful housing discrimination.
rules.citation: California Fair Employment and Housing Act (FEHA)
rules.quoted_span: Housing  providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system. Housing providers are also prohibited from having “blanket bans” of all people with a criminal history.

rules.title: Cambridge Tenants Rights and Resources Notification Ordinance
rules.requirement: Landlords and management companies must give tenants the Tenants Rights and Resources Guide at the start of a tenancy and when legal steps to terminate a tenancy are taken, such as a notice to quit.
rules.coverage_conditions: All residential rental agreements in Cambridge, including single dwelling units and tenancies at will; the Ordinance does not restrict when a landlord may evict.
rules.exemptions: Units in a hospital, skilled nursing or health facility; non-profit facilities whose primary purpose is short-term alcohol, drug or substance-abuse treatment; short-term rental units under the zoning ordinance.
rules.penalty: Fine of $300 for each day's violation.
rules.quoted_span: The Ordinance requires owners, landlords, and management companies to provide you with information at the start of your lease or tenancy as well as when your tenancy is being terminated.

rules.title: Hoboken Rent Leveling and Stabilization Ordinance rent increase cap
rules.requirement: A landlord may not raise rent by more than 5% or the CPI percentage differential, whichever is less, nor more than once in any 12-month period; tax, water/sewer and capital-improvement surcharges require approval.
rules.coverage_conditions: Rental dwellings under the Hoboken Rent Leveling and Stabilization chapter; newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984 may be exempt.
rules.exemptions: Newly constructed dwellings and buildings completely vacant since January 1, 1984 may be exempt, with eligibility determined by the Regulation Officer or Rent Regulation Officer.
rules.penalty: Excess rent increases are void and excess rents must be refunded or credited to the tenant.
rules.quoted_span:
At the expiration of a lease or at the termination of a lease of a periodic tenant, no landlord
     may request or receive a percentage increase in rent which is greater than 5% or the percentage
     difference between the consumer price index three months prior to the expiration or termination
     of the lease and three months prior to the commencement of the lease term, whichever is less.

rules.title: Los Angeles relocation assistance for no-fault evictions under the RSO and JCO
rules.requirement: For a no-fault eviction of a tenant in an RSO- or JCO-covered unit, the landlord must file a Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD before serving notice and pay relocation assistance within 15 days of service.
rules.coverage_conditions: All units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause Ordinance (JCO) in the City of Los Angeles.
rules.exemptions: Resident-manager replacement; eviction required by a natural-disaster hazard not caused by the landlord's negligence; landlord may offset the tenant's accumulated rent. Mom and Pop properties (four or fewer units) pay reduced amounts for owner, family or manager occupancy.
rules.penalty: Failure to file the Landlord Declaration makes the eviction a violation of the RSO or JCO; a tenant may raise non-payment of relocation assistance as an affirmative defense.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Rent Stabilization Ordinance (L.A.M.C. §151.00 et seq.); Los Angeles Just Cause Ordinance (L.A.M.C. §165.00 et seq.)
rules.quoted_span:
All tenant not- at-fault evictions require payment of relocation assistance and the filing of a 
Declaration of Intent to Evict form with the Los Angeles Housing Department (LAHD) before 
evicting tenants from units covered by the Rent Stabilization Ordinance (RSO) or the Just Cause 
Ordinance (JCO).

rules.title: Resident Protections Ordinance relocation for demolition of Protected Units
rules.requirement: An owner demolishing a Protected Unit for new construction must file a declaration or notice with LAHD, serve the relocation notice, and pay enhanced relocation assistance to lower-income tenants rather than the standard RSO or JCO amounts.
rules.coverage_conditions: Protected Units demolished for the purpose of new construction: rent-restricted, rent-controlled (including all RSO units), lower-income-occupied within the past five years, or Ellis Act withdrawn within the past ten years.
rules.exemptions: Units that are not Protected Units or are not occupied by a lower income tenant receive the regular RSO or JCO relocation amounts instead of the RPO-enhanced amounts.
rules.penalty: Failure to comply with the RPO may result in financial penalties starting at $250,000 per displaced unit and withholding of LAHD permit clearances.
rules.interaction: Owner must pay the higher of State HCA or City relocation amounts; RSO/JCO amounts must be enhanced for lower income tenants under the HCA.
rules.citation: Los Angeles Resident Protections Ordinance (L.A. Ordinances #188481, #188482)
rules.quoted_span:
Owners who demolish a Protected Unit for the purpose of new construction within 5 years after the 
filing of the Notice of Intent to Withdraw or Declaration of Intent to Evict with LAHD are required to 
comply with relocation requirements under the RPO.

rules.title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482) rent cap
rules.requirement: Annual rent increases for covered units are limited to 5% plus the regional cost-of-living change, or 10%, whichever is lower; the maximum allowable increase was 8.9% from August 1, 2024 to July 31, 2025 (previously 8.8%).
rules.coverage_conditions: Buildings older than 15 years, applied on a rolling basis. Excludes newer construction, deed-restricted affordable units, certain dormitories, owner-occupied two-unit properties, qualifying single-family homes and condominiums, and RSO units.
rules.exemptions: Units built within the last 15 years; deed-restricted affordable units; certain dormitories; two-unit properties with an owner-occupied second unit; qualifying single-family homes and condominiums; units already subject to the City's RSO.
